document.title: [Redacted] Noncommittal on Ariana Airlines Request (State Department Cable 05051)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Newly Published Documents Cast Doubt on Claims Taliban Will Give Up al Qaeda | National Security Archive
document.note: [Secret] Highly redacted cable to State headquarters reiterating that the UAE remained noncommittal on the US request to act against Ariana Airlines.

events.description: US Ambassador with Rep. LaHood and Consul General privately asked Dubai Crown Prince MBR to close down Ariana flights; MBR said he would consult advisors
Cable 03508 sent from Abu Dhabi reporting the demarche
US Embassy Abu Dhabi cable 03508 reports the Ambassador's discussion of GCC stance on Iran and the disputed islands.
US Ambassador, Consul General and Rep. LaHood met Dubai Crown Prince MBR to request halt of Ariana flights; MBR said he would consult advisors.
UAE State Security Director Shaykh Hazza made calls in Washington, accompanied by the Ambassador.
Cable 03508 sent from Embassy Abu Dhabi to State and NSC reporting MBR's response.
U.S. Embassy Abu Dhabi sent cable 3508 (section 3 of 5) to the State Department. The information copies went to the GCC posts, London, Paris, Doha, USCENTCOM, the NSC, SECDEF and DIA.

The Ambassador told UAE interlocutors that the US hoped the Saudi and UAE leaderships would resolve their differences directly, supported negotiation or arbitration over the disputed islands, and said the US was not in dialogue with Iran.
Shaykh Hazza held discussions in Washington shortly before the Ambassador's meeting.
Embassy Abu Dhabi transmitted cable 03508 (sections 3 and 4 of 5) on GCC stance on Iran and disputed islands to State, the NSC, DIA, and CENTCOM.

sources_cited: State Department cable Abu Dhabi 03508 (9 June 1999)
key_claims: The US asserted that UBL used Ariana Afghan Airlines to move men and materiel from Afghanistan via Dubai.
The US threatened to strike the Taliban hard and designate them a terrorist organization if UBL attacked Americans again.
The UAE's year-plus effort to moderate the Taliban and oust UBL had failed.
MBR demurred, calling closure ineffective, but promised to consult security advisors.
Ariana's main UAE operations were from Sharjah, with heavy cargo to Kandahar (940,956 kg Jan-May 1999).
The US Ambassador urged the Saudi and UAE leaderships to resolve their differences privately before they worsen.
The US supports a negotiated or arbitrated resolution of the disputed islands issue.
The Ambassador stressed that the US was not engaged in a dialogue with Iran, and that its offer to talk to Tehran was public.
This chunk has no jihadist-network content.
